q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM PRODUCT A LEFT JOIN CUSTOMER B ON A.PRODUCT_KEY = B.PRODUCT_KEY GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT B.PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 finds customers who have purchased all distinct products by comparing the count of distinct product keys for each customer against the total number of distinct products. Q2 joins PRODUCT and CUSTOMER and performs a similar check, but due to the LEFT JOIN, it may include customers who have no matching products, which can affect the GROUP BY and HAVING logic differently.
counterexample_dsp: A scenario where a customer has no product association but still appears in the result of Q2 due to LEFT JOIN, while Q1 correctly excludes them.
